---
title: "Widgets"
engine: julia
toc-depth: 3
---

Widgets are HTML controls deck.gl overlays on the canvas — zoom buttons, a compass, a
screenshot button, a popup. All 15 are available, generated from deck.gl's own prop
tables.

Pass them to `Deck` with the `widgets` keyword:

```julia
Deck(layer, widgets = [ZoomWidget(), CompassWidget()])
```

Widgets are styled by a deck.gl stylesheet that pages include only when they actually
contain a widget. Every example below sits on a Carto basemap, passed as `map_style` —
see [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd).

### Common Props

Every widget accepts these:

| Prop | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | per widget | Identifier, unique within a deck |
| `placement` | per widget | `"top-left"`, `"top-right"`, `"bottom-left"`, `"bottom-right"` |
| `style` | `Dict()` | Inline CSS, including the `--button-*` custom properties |
| `class_name` | `""` | Extra CSS class |
| `view_id` | `nothing` | Bind the widget to one view in a multi-view deck |

The tables below list what each widget adds on top of those.

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
using DeckGL

snake(prop::Symbol) = lowercase(replace(String(prop), r"([a-z0-9])([A-Z])" => s"\1_\2"))

# Shared by every widget and documented once, above.
const COMMON = [:_container, :className, :id, :placement, :style, :viewId]

# Generated rather than transcribed, so a deck.gl upgrade cannot leave these stale.
function widget_reference(T)
    name = DeckGL.typename(T)
    specific = filter(!in(COMMON), DeckGL.props(T))
    io = IOBuffer()
    println(io, "::: {.callout-note collapse=\"true\"}")
    println(io, "## `$name` props\n")
    if isempty(specific)
        println(io, "Only the common props above.")
    else
        println(io, "In addition to the common props:\n")
        println(io, "| Prop |")
        println(io, "|------|")
        for p in specific
            println(io, "| `", snake(p), "` |")
        end
    end
    println(io, "\nDescriptions and accepted values are in the ",
                "[deck.gl widget reference](https://deck.gl/docs/api-reference/widgets/",
                replace(snake(name), "_" => "-"), ").")
    println(io, ":::")
    return String(take!(io))
end

points = (
    lng  = [-122.45, -122.42, -122.38, -122.50, -122.47],
    lat  = [37.78, 37.76, 37.79, 37.77, 37.80],
    size = [80, 200, 120, 300, 150],
    name = ["Alpha", "Bravo", "Charlie", "Delta", "Echo"],
)

# One deck per example, differing only in its widgets.
demo(widgets...; kw...) = Deck(
    ScatterplotLayer(
        data = points,
        get_position = [:lng, :lat],
        get_radius = :size,
        get_fill_color = [255, 140, 0, 200],
        radius_min_pixels = 4,
        pickable = true,
    ),
    initial_view_state = ViewState(; longitude = -122.44, latitude = 37.77, zoom = 12, kw...),
    map_style = "https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/gl/positron-gl-style/style.json",
    widgets = collect(widgets),
)

# `icon` props take an image URL. These SVGs are inlined so the page needs nothing.
star_icon = "data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8," *
    "<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 24 24'>" *
    "<path fill='black' d='M12 2l3 7h7l-5.5 4.5L18 21l-6-4-6 4 1.5-7.5L2 9h7z'/></svg>"
dot_icon = "data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8," *
    "<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 24 24'>" *
    "<circle cx='12' cy='12' r='8' fill='black'/></svg>"
```

## Camera {#camera}

### ZoomWidget

Zoom in and out buttons.

```{julia}
demo(ZoomWidget())
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(ZoomWidget))
```

Lay the buttons out horizontally and move them:

```{julia}
demo(ZoomWidget(placement = "bottom-left", orientation = "horizontal",
                transition_duration = 400))
```

### CompassWidget

A compass rose showing the current bearing. Click it to reset to north, then to flatten
the pitch.

```{julia}
demo(CompassWidget(); pitch = 45, bearing = -30)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(CompassWidget))
```

### GimbalWidget

Pitch and bearing together, drawn as a gimbal. Click to reset both.

```{julia}
demo(GimbalWidget(); pitch = 50, bearing = 20)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(GimbalWidget))
```

### ResetViewWidget

Returns the camera to where it started. Give it an explicit `initial_view_state` to reset
somewhere other than the deck's own.

```{julia}
demo(ResetViewWidget(), ZoomWidget())
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(ResetViewWidget))
```

### ScrollbarWidget

A scrollbar that pans the view within `content_bounds`, given as two corners,
`[[min_lng, min_lat], [max_lng, max_lat]]`.

```{julia}
demo(
    ScrollbarWidget(content_bounds = [[-122.6, 37.6], [-122.3, 37.9]],
                    orientation = "vertical", placement = "top-right"),
    ScrollbarWidget(id = "scroll-x", content_bounds = [[-122.6, 37.6], [-122.3, 37.9]],
                    orientation = "horizontal", placement = "bottom-left"),
)
```

Two widgets of the same type need distinct `id`s, as above.

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(ScrollbarWidget))
```

## Display {#display}

### FullscreenWidget

Expands the deck's container to fill the screen.

```{julia}
demo(FullscreenWidget())
```

In a notebook or on this page the deck lives in an iframe, so fullscreen applies to that
frame.

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(FullscreenWidget))
```

### ThemeWidget

Switches the widgets between light and dark. `initial_theme_mode` may be `"auto"`,
`"light"`, or `"dark"`; `light_mode_theme` and `dark_mode_theme` hold the CSS custom
properties each mode applies.

```{julia}
demo(ThemeWidget(initial_theme_mode = "auto"), ZoomWidget(), CompassWidget())
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(ThemeWidget))
```

### ScreenshotWidget

Downloads the canvas as an image.

```{julia}
demo(ScreenshotWidget(filename = "map.png", image_format = "image/png"))
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(ScreenshotWidget))
```

### LoadingWidget

A spinner shown while any layer is still fetching data. It stays hidden otherwise, so it
is invisible on a deck whose data is already embedded.

```{julia}
demo(LoadingWidget(label = "Loading…"))
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(LoadingWidget))
```

## Information {#information}

### InfoWidget

A tooltip anchored to the picked object. `get_tooltip` is a JavaScript function of the
[picking info](https://deck.gl/docs/developer-guide/interactivity), and `mode` is
`"hover"` or `"click"`.

```{julia}
demo(InfoWidget(
    mode = "click",
    get_tooltip = JS("info => info.index >= 0 ? {html: `<b>index</b> \${info.index}`} : null"),
))
```

For the common case of showing a few columns, the layer's `tooltip` prop is simpler — it
ships the columns for you and needs no JavaScript:

```julia
ScatterplotLayer(data = points, get_position = [:lng, :lat], tooltip = [:name, :size])
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(InfoWidget))
```

### PopupWidget

A popup pinned to a coordinate. `content` is HTML.

```{julia}
demo(PopupWidget(
    position = [-122.44, 37.77],
    content = "<b>Downtown</b><br>Pinned to a coordinate.",
    default_is_open = true,
    close_button = true,
))
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(PopupWidget))
```

### ContextMenuWidget

A right-click menu. Each entry is a `label` and a `key`, and `on_menu_item_selected`
receives the key.

```{julia}
demo(ContextMenuWidget(
    menu_items = [
        Dict("label" => "Zoom in",   "key" => "zoom-in"),
        Dict("label" => "Copy point", "key" => "copy"),
    ],
    on_menu_item_selected = JS("key => console.log('selected', key)"),
))
```

Right-click the map to open it.

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(ContextMenuWidget))
```

## Custom Controls {#custom-controls}

These three are building blocks: they render a control and hand the event back to
JavaScript, so what they do is up to you.

### IconWidget

A button with your own icon. `icon` is an image URL — a file, or an inlined SVG as here.

```{julia}
demo(IconWidget(
    icon = star_icon,
    label = "Say hello",
    on_click = JS("() => console.log('icon widget clicked')"),
))
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(IconWidget))
```

### ToggleWidget

A two-state button, with a separate icon and label for the on state.

```{julia}
demo(ToggleWidget(
    icon = dot_icon,    label = "Markers off",
    on_icon = star_icon, on_label = "Markers on",
    initial_checked = false,
    on_change = JS("checked => console.log('checked:', checked)"),
))
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(ToggleWidget))
```

### SelectorWidget

A dropdown. `options` is a list of `label`/`value` pairs.

```{julia}
demo(SelectorWidget(
    options = [
        Dict("label" => "Orange", "value" => "orange"),
        Dict("label" => "Blue",   "value" => "blue"),
    ],
    initial_value = "orange",
    on_change = JS("value => console.log('picked', value)"),
))
```

Reacting to a selection means changing layer props from JavaScript. For anything driven
from Julia, rebuild the `Deck` and re-render instead.

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println(widget_reference(SelectorWidget))
```

## Combining Widgets

Widgets stack in the order given, grouped by `placement`.

```{julia}
demo(
    ZoomWidget(placement = "top-left"),
    CompassWidget(placement = "top-left"),
    ResetViewWidget(placement = "top-left"),
    FullscreenWidget(placement = "top-right"),
    ScreenshotWidget(placement = "top-right"),
    ThemeWidget(placement = "bottom-right");
    pitch = 40, bearing = -25,
)
```

## Every Widget

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
using DeckGL: WIDGET_NAMES
println("Generated from deck.gl v", DeckGL.DECKGL_VERSION, ":\n")
println("| Widget | Extra props |")
println("|--------|-------------|")
for name in WIDGET_NAMES
    extra = filter(!in(COMMON), DeckGL.props(getfield(DeckGL, name)))
    println("| `", name, "` | ", isempty(extra) ? "—" : join(("`" * snake(p) * "`" for p in extra), ", "), " |")
end
```
